title: Uncut Gems: Gemcutting Skill and Support Gems in PoE 2
summary: In Path of Exile 2 you do not find finished skill gems - you find Uncut Skill Gems and Uncut Support Gems, then 'cut' them at the Gemcutter's Workshop into the exact gem you want (gated by attribute and level). This guide covers tiers, how to cut, and how to upgrade uncut gems.
description: A source-linked reference for Uncut Gems in Path of Exile 2: the Uncut Skill Gem and Uncut Support Gem system, gemcutting, tiers, and upgrading.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Uncut Gems - uncut skill and support gems that are cut into specific gems at the Gemcutter's Workshop

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Right-click an Uncut Skill Gem (or Uncut Support Gem) to open the Gemcutter's Workshop, then pick the exact gem you meet the attribute and level requirements for. Higher-tier uncut gems produce higher-level gems. You can also upgrade an uncut gem to a higher tier before cutting.
calloutDetail: Uncut gems replace random gem drops - you choose the gem, not the RNG.
You can only cut a gem whose attribute/level requirement you currently meet; others show locked until you qualify.

sections.title: Uncut gem families
intro: There are two uncut families - skill and support - each in tiers. A higher tier uncut gem yields a higher-level finished gem. The exact tier-to-level mapping can shift between patches; treat the in-game Workshop as the source of truth.

members.title: Uncut Skill Gem
body: Cut at the Workshop into any skill gem you meet the requirements for. Tier sets the resulting gem level.

members.title: Uncut Support Gem
body: Cut into any support gem you qualify for; supports modify the skills they are linked to.

members.title: Gem tiers
body: Higher tiers produce higher-level gems. You can upgrade a lower uncut gem toward a higher tier before cutting.

sections.title: What you can cut
note: You can only cut a gem whose attribute and level requirement you currently meet. Unmet gems stay locked in the Workshop until you qualify.

sections.title: How to get Uncut Gems
intro: Uncut gems are handed out as you progress and drop throughout the game.

routes.label: Quest rewards
body: Main-story and side quests grant Uncut Skill and Support Gems as you unlock the gem system.

routes.label: Monster / map drops
body: Uncut gems drop from monsters and endgame content, with tier scaling by area level.

routes.label: Vendor / Gem Stash
body: Some NPCs and the shared Gem Stash let you manage, store and sometimes redeem gems.

routes.label: Currency upgrade
body: Use a gem-upgrade currency to raise an uncut gem's tier before cutting.

steps.label: Open the Workshop
body: Right-click the Uncut Gem (or use the Gem Stash) to open the Gemcutter's Workshop.

steps.label: Pick the gem
body: Browse skills or supports; only those you qualify for are selectable.

steps.label: Confirm tier
body: Higher uncut tier yields a higher-level gem - confirm before cutting.

steps.label: Cut
body: Confirm to convert the uncut gem into the chosen gem, added to your Gem Stash.

sections.title: How uncut gems interact with skills
paragraphs: Uncut gems are the delivery mechanism for your entire skill kit. Instead of hoping a specific gem drops, you hold an Uncut Skill Gem and cut it into the exact skill your build needs at the Workshop.

Support gems work the same way: an Uncut Support Gem becomes the support that modifies a linked skill. Because you choose supports deliberately, you plan your support setup around the gems you can actually cut.

Attribute and level requirements gate the choice. A Strength gem stays locked until your build has enough Strength; an Intelligence-locked support waits until you qualify. This is why uncut gems are also a build-planning tool: the gems you can cut right now reflect your current attribute spread.

Finished gems live in the shared Gem Stash, where you socket them into weapons, armour and amulets. Upgrading an uncut gem's tier before cutting is the main way to reach higher gem levels without finding a higher-tier drop.
bullets: Uncut Skill Gem -> chosen skill gem.
Uncut Support Gem -> chosen support gem.
Attribute/level gating makes uncut gems a build-planning signal.
Upgrade tier before cutting for higher gem level.
Finished gems go to the shared Gem Stash for socketing.

sections.title: Uncut gems vs other paths
paragraphs: In Path of Exile 1, finished skill gems dropped from monsters and vendors. Path of Exile 2 replaces that with uncut gems: you always choose the gem, so there is no 'wrong drop' frustration - but you also cannot stockpile a finished gem you do not yet qualify for.
Compared to buying a gem from an NPC, uncut gems are the default path in PoE2; vendors and the Gem Stash are secondary ways to manage or redeem gems. The choice still lives in the Workshop.

Against simply keeping a higher-tier uncut gem, cutting early lets you use the skill now, while holding a high-tier uncut gem delays power until you cut it. Balance immediate need against the higher gem level a top tier would give.
bullets: PoE1: finished gems drop. PoE2: you cut uncut gems (no wrong drops).
Vendors/Gem Stash are secondary to the Workshop.
Cut early for use now, or hold high tier for a stronger gem later.

entries.question: The skill gem I want is locked in the Workshop - why?
summary: A player could not cut the gem they wanted.
editorialAnalysis: The gem's attribute or level requirement is not met. It stays locked until the build qualifies (more attribute points or a higher level).
officialAnswer: Meet the gem's attribute/level requirement, then cut it.

entries.question: Should I upgrade the uncut gem's tier before cutting?
editorialAnalysis: Higher-tier uncut gems produce higher-level finished gems. If you want the strongest version, upgrade the tier before cutting; if you need the skill now, cut at the tier you have.
officialAnswer: Upgrade tier for a higher gem level; cut at current tier for immediate use.
